findings.description: `_ADAPTERS_DIR` is derived from `__file__` using two `dirname()` calls and then appending `.claude/adapters`. In this diff-touched file, `__file__` is already under `.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/providers`, so the computed path becomes `.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/.claude/adapters`, not the real adapters root. Any `--transport claude-headless` path that calls `_adapters()` will insert the wrong directory into `sys.path` and then fail to import `loa_cheval`.
findings.failure_mode: Running the new claude-headless probe transport fails before probing with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'loa_cheval'`, so FR-3’s CLI transport is unusable from this file location.
findings.suggested_fix: Compute the adapters root as the directory above `loa_cheval`, e.g. from this file use `os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))`, or otherwise reuse an existing repo-root/adapters-root resolver instead of appending `.claude/adapters` below `loa_cheval`.

findings.description: A token-budget 429 (ceiling.is_token_limit_message) is returned as kind=transient with token_limit=True; in step() when it persists over the 3 attempts (backoffs total 20s) the sample is rewritten to kind=size, failure_class=token_limit, size_origin=provider. The bisection then treats a per-minute input-token throttle as a context rejection: it becomes smallest_fail, brackets the previous accept, and _outcome_reasons reports `clean`. With --write-catalog the entry is written as method: probed_headless from a rate-limit artifact. The written value is still an accepted, needle-verified size (so the bound is conservative, never too high), but it is labeled clean and will under-report the route's real ceiling by whatever the org's ITPM happened to allow in that minute.
findings.failure_mode: An org below the top rate tier probing a 1M-window model: a large step is accepted (consuming the minute's budget), the next step hits the token 429 three times inside ~20s, is recorded as a size rejection, the bracket closes within tolerance, outcome=clean, and the catalog gets an ITPM-bounded effective_input_ceiling with no partial flag.
findings.suggested_fix: Never let a failure_class=token_limit sample satisfy the bracket: in _outcome_reasons add a reason when the smallest_fail sample's failure_class != context_limit (or exclude token_limit samples from current_fail and keep them as `other`-class stops). Alternatively lengthen the token_limit backoff to cover a full 60s window before giving up.

findings.description: step() charges `est = (measured or est_measured) * price_in // 1_000_000` for every attempt, including size rejections with size_origin=cli_local (the CLI's own pre-flight, no provider call, no billing) and OSError before spawn. The live run shows the effect: estimate $19.10 vs CLI-reported $12.74, and the $20 cap stopped the bisection (`outcome: partial`) while real spend had ~$7 of headroom. The two CLI pre-flight rejections (filler 1,000,000 and 590,000 at $4/MTok) alone account for ~$6.36 of phantom spend.
findings.failure_mode: The budget pre-check (`spent_micro + est_measured * price_in // 1_000_000 > budget_micro`) trips early, producing partial outcomes and no catalog write on runs that were in fact well within budget; operators then hand-write the catalog, which is exactly what happened in Task 1.5.
findings.suggested_fix: In step(), when res['kind']=='size' and res.get('size_origin')=='cli_local' (and for the OSError branch) charge 0 (or only rep_micro if the CLI reported a cost). Keep the full estimate for timeouts and provider-side errors, where the input may have been billed.

findings.description: `diag` is truncated to 300 characters before any classification: `is_context_limit_message(diag)`, `is_token_limit_message(diag)`, `_PROVIDER_ORIGIN.search(diag)`, `parse_context_limit(diag)` and the _TRANSIENT_MARKERS scan all run on the clipped string. The diag is assembled as result + api_status + stderr, so when the CLI emits a preamble (warnings, a JSON-wrapped API error envelope, Bedrock's `ValidationException: The model returned the following errors: ...` prefix) the limit statement or its token count can fall past the cut.
findings.failure_mode: A genuine context-limit rejection is classified as `other` (bisection stops, outcome partial, exit 1) or its `rejected_input_tokens` is lost (size_basis degrades to `scaled` and the ratio is not corrected), after the step's tokens were already paid for.
findings.suggested_fix: Classify on the untruncated diag and apply the `[:300]` only to the `detail` stored in the returned dict.

findings.description: step() guards `_run_capped` + `_classify` only against subprocess.TimeoutExpired and OSError. Any other exception from the classification path (e.g. `ceiling.parse_context_limit(diag)` returning None → AttributeError on `.get`, a non-int value flowing into `_size`/`max`, a JSON type surprise in `usage`) propagates out of _main_cli with a traceback. The record — the only artifact of the money already spent, and what the SDD says is 'always written' — is built and written only after the loop, so it is lost.
findings.failure_mode: A probe that has consumed several multi-dollar steps dies on an unanticipated classifier exception; no record file, no samples, no spent_usd, and the operator cannot tell what was learned or billed.
findings.suggested_fix: In step(), catch `Exception` around `_classify` (and `_run_capped`) and convert to `{'kind': 'other', 'detail': f'classifier error: {e!r}'}`; additionally write the record in a `try/finally` so a crash after the first attempt still persists what was measured.

findings.description: Catalog-write prerequisites are checked only after the bisection has spent its budget: i2_clamped raises when the entry has no positive context_window, and write_catalog_operator_set raises when `effective_input_ceiling:`, `probed_ceiling:` or `ceiling_calibration:` is absent at indent 8 — the normal state of a never-calibrated entry, i.e. the main use case for a probe. The failure surfaces as `catalog not written` / exit 1 after a clean (paid) run. Separately, `--allow-partial`, `--tier` and `--itpm` are accepted by argparse but silently ignored when `--transport claude-headless`; an operator passing `--allow-partial --write-catalog` (the Task 1.5 situation) gets no write and no warning.
findings.failure_mode: A $20 clean probe of a fresh model entry ends with 'catalog not written: … `ceiling_calibration` not found in the entry'; or an operator relies on --allow-partial and discovers after the run that it had no effect on this transport.
findings.suggested_fix: At the top of _main_cli, when --write-catalog is set, read the catalog and run i2_clamped plus a dry write_catalog_operator_set with a placeholder ceiling (discarding the result) to fail fast before any spend. Either honor --allow-partial on the headless path or make argparse reject --allow-partial/--tier/--itpm with --transport claude-headless.

findings.description: `subprocess.run(..., timeout=timeout)` kills only the direct child on TimeoutExpired. The documented route runs through a wrapper (`claude-bedrock`, CLAUDE_HEADLESS_BIN); unless that wrapper `exec`s the CLI, SIGKILL on the wrapper leaves the real `claude` node process alive to finish the ~1M-token request. step() then classifies the timeout as transient, sleeps 5s, and sends the same prompt again.
findings.failure_mode: On a slow step two or three concurrent 1M-token requests run against the same account: billed input the budget accounting never sees, plus self-inflicted 429s that the next attempt may record as a token_limit → size rejection (see DISS-001).
findings.suggested_fix: Launch with `start_new_session=True` and on TimeoutExpired send `os.killpg(proc.pid, SIGKILL)` (use Popen + communicate(timeout=) rather than subprocess.run), then re-raise; also rmtree the workspace after the group is dead.

findings.description: For a ProviderUnavailableError the transient decision includes `_STATUS_5XX.search(diag)` with pattern `\b5\d\d\b` over the free-text diag. Any word-delimited 3-digit number starting with 5 matches: node stack-trace positions (`cli.js:512:13`), line counts, ids. A deterministic CLI crash on a large prompt (OOM, a thrown error with a stack) whose stderr contains such a number is retried as transient.
findings.failure_mode: Two extra full-size attempts (each charged at est, ~$4 per 1M-token step at the catalog price) plus 20s of backoff for an error that cannot succeed, draining the budget cap and pushing the run to partial.
findings.suggested_fix: Anchor the 5xx match to a status context, e.g. `(?:status|http|error)[ :=]+5\d\d\b` or `\b5\d\d\b(?=\s*(?:internal|service|bad gateway|overloaded))`, mirroring how _PROVIDER_ORIGIN already requires explicit markers.
